title: Novena for Relief from Debt and Financial Hardship
kicker: 9 days of trust in God’s providence
card: For anyone carrying debt or money worries: 9 days of trust, honest work and wise stewardship.
ogDescription: 9 days of prayer for relief from debt and financial hardship, through St. Joseph, St. Rita and St. Jude.
description: A 9-day Catholic novena for relief from debt and financial hardship, through St. Joseph, St. Rita of Cascia and St. Jude Thaddeus.

epigraph.text: Cast all your anxieties on him, for he cares about you.

closingVerse.text: But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things shall be yours as well.

saints.name: St. Joseph
saints.bio: Carpenter of Nazareth and foster-father of Jesus, who provided for the Holy Family by honest labor. Invoked for steady work and trust in God’s provision.
saints.alt: Painting: St. Joseph holding the Infant Jesus, by Guido Reni

saints.name: St. Rita of Cascia
saints.bio: Wife, mother, widow and Augustinian nun who bore long family trials with patience and forgiveness, and became a peacemaker in her town.
saints.alt: Painting: St. Rita of Cascia, from her 15th-century coffin

saints.name: St. Jude Thaddeus
saints.bio: Apostle and martyr, traditionally linked to the Letter of Jude. Long invoked by the faithful when all seems hopeless.
saints.alt: Painting: St. Jude Thaddeus, by Anthony van Dyck

openingPrayer: Heavenly Father, You know every financial burden we carry and every debt that weighs on our minds. We place our trust in Your loving providence rather than in our own fear. Today we ask St. Joseph, faithful guardian and provider; St. Rita of Cascia, advocate of the impossible; and St. Jude Thaddeus, patron of desperate cases, to join their prayers with ours before Your throne, through Christ our Lord.
closingPrayer: Lord Jesus, guide our steps, bless our honest work, grant us wisdom in stewardship, and lead us to freedom from debt according to Your holy will.

memorare.text: Remember, O most chaste spouse of the Virgin Mary, that never was it known that anyone who implored your help and sought your intercession was left unassisted. Full of confidence in your power, I fly unto you and beg your protection. Despise not, O Guardian of the Redeemer, my humble supplication, but in your bounty, hear and answer me.

tips.p: One person leads each part; all respond pray for us and Amen, and say the closing prayers together. The prayers say “we”; if you pray alone, say “I”.
If you can, go to Confession and attend Mass during these 9 days, and pair prayer with prudent action: an honest budget, a talk with creditors, wise counsel (Day 4).

days.title: Surrendering Financial Fear
days.refl: Jesus does not tell us our needs are imaginary. He tells us they are known. When the angel woke St. Joseph in the night, he rose and led Mary and the Child into Egypt with no plan beyond the next road. He did not see the whole way; he trusted the One who did. Fear wants to carry tomorrow today. Faith carries today, and leaves tomorrow with the Father.
days.more: Feeling anxious about money is not a sin; it is a weight that faith is invited to set down. Jesus speaks to people who really did worry about food and clothing. He calls them “of little faith” with tenderness, not contempt, and turns their eyes to a Father who already knows. St. Joseph’s silence in the Gospels is not emptiness but trust: he listens, then acts. We can begin the same way, naming our fears honestly before God instead of rehearsing them alone at night.
days.step: Write your money worries on one sheet, pray over it, and fold it away as a sign of handing them to God.
days.prayer: Heavenly Father, You know what we need before we ask. Fear about money and unpaid debts often steals our sleep and our peace. Through the intercession of St. Joseph, who trusted You on the road to Egypt, help us lay our anxieties in Your hands. Give us calm hearts, clear minds and the courage to face our situation one honest step at a time.
days.verse: Therefore do not be anxious, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’ For the Gentiles seek all these things; and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.

days.title: Hope When Options Run Out
days.refl: The angel told a young woman with no power and no money that “with God nothing will be impossible.” Mary did not have answers; she had trust, and she said yes. St. Rita lived through years when every door seemed shut, and St. Jude has long been invoked by people who feel they have run out of options. Their lives say the same thing: God’s mercy is larger than our calculations.
days.more: Hope is different from optimism. Optimism looks at the numbers and expects them to improve; hope looks at God and trusts Him whatever the numbers say. Mary’s “let it be to me” was not passive resignation but an active yes, given before she could see how things would work out. Tradition tells that St. Rita was refused entry to the convent at Cascia three times, yet she kept praying, and worked to reconcile the feuding families, until the way opened. Hope keeps knocking, gently and persistently, without despair.
days.step: Choose one door to knock on this week, like a call or a request for advice, and pray for courage.
days.prayer: Lord God, nothing is impossible for You. When our debts look too heavy and the numbers will not add up, renew our hope in Your power to open doors we cannot see. With Mary, who said yes without knowing the way, and with St. Rita praying beside us, guard our home from despair and show us the next faithful step.
days.verse: And Mary said, “Behold, I am the handmaid of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.” And the angel departed from her.

days.title: Blessing on Daily Work
days.refl: In the workshop at Nazareth, St. Joseph measured, cut and sanded, and the Son of God learned a trade at his side. Ordinary, honest work became holy there. The psalm calls it a blessing to eat the fruit of the labor of our hands. Work is not only how we pay what we owe; it is one of the ways God answers our prayer for daily bread.
days.more: The Church honors St. Joseph the Worker on May 1, reminding us that labor has dignity because it shares in God’s own work of creating and sustaining. A job that feels small is still a place where God can be served and found. If work is scarce, our search for it can itself be offered as prayer. If work is hard, we can ask St. Joseph to pray for us as we work, for he once worked beside Jesus: faithfully, patiently and without cutting corners.
days.step: Before work or your job search today, pray: “St. Joseph the Worker, pray for us,” and offer the day to God.
days.prayer: Father, bless the work of our hands. Bring steady, honest income into our home, and lead us to fair work and good opportunities. Through the prayers of St. Joseph, the faithful carpenter of Nazareth, help us work with diligence and integrity, so that we may provide for those we love and pay what we owe with honest hearts.
days.verse: Blessed is every one who fears the LORD, / who walks in his ways! / You shall eat the fruit of the labor of your hands; / you shall be happy, and it shall be well with you.

days.title: Wisdom in Stewardship
days.refl: Jesus points to the builder who first sits down and counts the cost. Faith does not avoid budgets or hard numbers; it gives us the courage to look at them. Prayer and prudence walk together. Facing every debt honestly, spending with care and seeking good advice are not signs of weak faith. They are how we cooperate with the grace we are asking for.
days.more: Prudence is one of the cardinal virtues: the practical wisdom to see what is true and choose the right means to a good end. Paying what we owe is a matter of justice, so a realistic plan is itself an act of faithfulness and love. It can be humbling to ask for counsel, from a trusted friend, the parish social action ministry or a professional, but humility receives the help that pride refuses. God often answers prayer through wise people He places on our path.
days.step: List every debt on one page with its amount, due date and interest; seeing the whole picture is where a plan begins.
days.prayer: God of wisdom, give us clear eyes to face every debt honestly, and the discipline to spend, save and plan with care. Help us recognize wise counsel and accept it with humility. Free us from careless choices and from the shame that makes us hide, and lead us patiently toward the freedom of an ordered life.
days.verse: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost, whether he has enough to complete it?

days.title: Patience in Waiting
days.refl: Getting out of debt rarely happens overnight. Some burdens lift slowly, payment by payment. St. Rita knew long waiting: a marriage shadowed by family feuds, the loss of her husband and sons, and years of prayer that never let bitterness take root. To wait quietly for the Lord is not to give up. It is to keep doing the next good thing while trusting Him with the timing.
days.more: Waiting tempts us in two directions: to despair (“nothing will change”) or to rush (“I must fix everything now, whatever it takes”). Both forget that God is at work in time. St. Rita’s patience was not weakness; tradition remembers how she forgave those who had wronged her family. Patience grows when we measure progress honestly, celebrate small steps and refuse quick fixes that only deepen debt: gambling, high-interest “5-6” loans or lending apps, and get-rich schemes.
days.step: When frustration rises today, pause and pray one Hail Mary slowly before you speak or decide.
days.prayer: Lord, when progress feels slow and we grow tired of waiting for relief, strengthen our perseverance. Keep us from discouragement, from bitterness, and from quick schemes that only make our burdens heavier. Through the prayers of St. Rita, who waited on You through long years, guard our hearts and keep us faithful one day at a time.
days.verse: The LORD is good to those who wait for him, / to the soul that seeks him. / It is good that one should wait quietly / for the salvation of the LORD.

days.title: Peace for the Family
days.refl: Money strain often spills into the home: sharp words, silence, blame. St. Joseph guarded the peace of the Holy Family through danger and uncertainty, and St. Rita became known as a peacemaker in a town divided by feuds. St. Paul asks us to put on love, which binds everything together, and to let the peace of Christ rule in our hearts. Our debts do not have to divide us.
days.more: Financial stress is one of the most common sources of tension in families. Peace does not mean pretending everything is fine; it means facing problems together, as a team rather than as opponents. It helps to speak gently, to share the facts openly among the adults, to tell children only what they can carry, and to forgive quickly. Children notice how we carry hard things. When they see us pray, plan and stay kind under pressure, they learn a faith that will serve them for life.
days.step: Spend a few minutes together today without talking about money, and thank one another for one specific thing.
days.prayer: Loving Father, protect our family from the strain of money worries. Where there has been blame, bring forgiveness; where there has been silence, bring honest words spoken with love. Through the prayers of St. Joseph, guardian of the Holy Family, and St. Rita the peacemaker, fill our home with patience, mutual support and the peace of Christ in every trial.
days.verse: And above all these put on love, which binds everything together in perfect harmony. And let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, to which indeed you were called in the one body. And be thankful.

days.title: Pressing Bills & Deadlines
days.refl: St. Paul wrote these words while in chains, not from comfort. He does not pretend our troubles are small; he tells us to turn every worry into prayer, with thanksgiving. When bills and deadlines press close, we can do exactly that, by name. St. Jude, patron of desperate cases, is a friend in urgent need: we ask him to pray for us as we face our most pressing bills.
days.more: Notice the order St. Paul gives: prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, and then peace. Thanksgiving in the middle of pressure seems strange, yet it reminds us of every time God has already carried us through. St. John’s Gospel shows Jude, “not Iscariot,” asking Jesus a sincere question at the Last Supper (John 14:22), and the faithful have long invited him into the hardest cases. Peace that “passes all understanding” does not wait for the bills to be paid; it keeps our hearts while we deal with them.
days.step: Contact the creditor of your most urgent bill: pay what you can after essentials, or ask for a fair written arrangement.
days.prayer: Lord Jesus, You know the exact obligations and urgent bills pressing on us right now. We bring them to You by name, with thanks for every time You have provided for us before. Through the prayers of St. Jude, friend in urgent need, provide timely relief, fair arrangements and the means to meet our commitments, and guard our hearts with Your peace.
days.verse: Have no anxiety about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which passes all understanding, will keep your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.

days.title: A Free & Generous Heart
days.refl: Just after telling us to pay everyone what is due, St. Paul names the only debt we should never stop paying: love. Freedom from debt is not about having more for ourselves; it is about being free to give what we owe, and then to give generously. Money is a good servant and a cruel master. As this burden lifts, we ask for hearts that stay humble, grateful and open to the needs of others.
days.more: Jesus warned that we cannot serve God and money. Borrowing is not a sin in itself, and repaying honestly is justice; but debt must not become our master. The goal of this novena is freedom: to owe nothing but love. Generosity is possible even in hard times; it may cost time or skill rather than cash. When we give, we remember that everything we have is gift. Beware of any message that promises riches in return for faith or offerings; God is a Father, not a merchant.
days.step: Do one small act of generosity that costs time rather than money: help, visit, listen, or pray for someone else’s burden.
days.prayer: Heavenly Father, purify our desires. As You lift this burden, keep our hearts humble and free from greed, envy and fear. Teach us to owe no one anything except love. Make us faithful stewards of all You give, generous to those in need, and grateful for every gift, great and small.
days.verse: Owe no one anything, except to love one another; for he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

days.title: Gratitude & Complete Trust in God’s Will
days.refl: A novena is a school of trust. We end these nine days not by demanding an outcome, but by giving thanks, because God hears every prayer and answers in the way that is truly best. Some answers come quickly, some slowly, some in forms we did not expect. With St. Joseph, St. Rita and St. Jude, we place our finances, our work and our future in the hands of a faithful Father.
days.more: Gratitude changes how we see. Looking back over these nine days, we may notice small graces: a kind word, an unexpected help, a clearer plan, a calmer heart. These are signs that God is at work. To trust His will is not to stop praying or planning; it is to keep doing both in peace. If you can, go to Confession and Mass in the days ahead and bring this intention to the altar, where Christ offers Himself for us.
days.step: Write down three graces you noticed during these nine days, and thank God for them together.
days.prayer: Lord, on this ninth day we thank You for Your faithfulness and for every grace, seen and unseen, that You have given and will give. Thank you, St. Joseph, St. Rita and St. Jude, for carrying our intentions before Jesus. We surrender our finances, our work and our future to Your loving will, trusting that You will provide what is truly good for us.
days.verse: Rejoice always, pray constantly, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.

printClosing: But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness,
and all these things shall be yours as well.
